messages.subject: treedepth vs n_leapfrog
parts:
Generically treedepth reports the size of the NUTS tree accepted
at each iteration but there is some ambiguity in what the number
of leapfrog steps should be. There are three options

1) 2^{treedepth} = number of states that could have been sampled
in the valid NUTS proposal.

2) 2^{treedepth} - 1 = number of new states that could have been
sampled in the valid NUTS proposal.

3) Number of gradient evaluations. This would also count the leapfrog
steps in any subtrees that are rejected in each NUTS proposal.

Does anyone have any strong feelings one way or another?

> Generically treedepth reports the size of the NUTS tree accepted

> of leapfrog steps should be. There are three options
>
> 1) 2^{treedepth} = number of states that could have been sampled
> in the valid NUTS proposal.
>
> 2) 2^{treedepth} - 1 = number of new states that could have been
> sampled in the valid NUTS proposal.
>
> 3) Number of gradient evaluations. This would also count the leapfrog
> steps in any subtrees that are rejected in each NUTS proposal.
>
> Does anyone have any strong feelings one way or another?

If (1) and (2) are derivable from treedepth, then (3) seems more
relevant. Also, if the point is to measure how much computation
was required, then (3) is the best proxy.

- Bob
